headline: Every bag checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: With oats and stockfeed going into similar bags, every bag needs the right label and batch code. Here's what a camera check could look like after your bagger. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bag is closed straight across, with no open corners or split tops. A bag that opens in the truck or the shed means wasted feed and a call from the farm.
labelLede: Rolled oats and oaten pellets go into bags that look the same from the outside. The camera checks every bag carries the right label for what is inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The batch code is how a bag is traced back to the mill. The system reads the printed batch code and date on every bag and compares them with the product and batch set at changeover.
objectLede: String, bag offcuts and pallet splinters can all end up on the bag conveyor. The camera spots anything that should not be there before bags are stacked.

vocab.alert: Four crooked closures in fifteen minutes. Check the bag closer.
